$comment: Returned Fire - game settings.
This file is the game's defaults. Edit it and it applies on the next reload (a dev server
picks it up straight away; a built copy lives next to index.html).
Settings changed in the title screen's settings column are remembered in localStorage and
layered on top of this file; bump `rev` below to throw those stored choices away (which is
what makes an edit here take effect for a player who already changed something). The URL
query parameters (?cpu=, ?quality=, ?seed= ...) override both - they are the test harness.
Everything under `tuning` is a simulation number, keyed by the dotted paths the engine
publishes (`rules.*`, `weapons.*`, `vehicles.*`). List only what you want to change: any
key you leave out keeps its compiled-in value. Units: speeds m/s, times seconds, ranges
metres, angles radians. `node tools/config-options.mjs` prints the full list of names.

video.$comment: Render quality preset: low / medium / high. Sets pixel ratio, shadow map size, bloom, MSAA and terrain bake resolution.

audio.$comment: 0..1. Master affects every bus including engines and effects; music is the score only. These are the values the mixer starts at, and the settings column reads them back, so the sliders show what is actually playing.

match.$comment: The title screen's match options. `cpu` is the enemy commander's build rate and reserve; `sandbox` is the practice range with no enemy force; `allies` fields a friendly CPU garrison.
match.$comment_map: `map` is an index into the map list, or -1 to pick one on the first match. `mode`: classic (procedural) or mirror (the older half-mirrored generator). `size`: small / medium / big.
match.$comment_vehicles: Garage choice for player one and player two (vkind: 1 jeep, 2 tank, 3 MLRS, 4 helicopter).
match.$comment_maxveh: Per-team ceiling on concurrent CPU hulls. 0 = the difficulty's own rule (2/3/6).

runtime.$comment: `fps` caps the frame rate (0 = uncapped). `look` selects the vehicle team-identity look: 0 stock (original painted marks), 1 bold hull bands, 2 team pennants, 3 team-coloured ground rings (the default - fliers keep camo and marks only).

$comment: Simulation numbers. Anything omitted keeps the compiled-in default, so a short list is
normal and is the recommended way to use this block. Examples:
"rules.rounds_to_win": 1,            captures needed to take a round
"rules.max_drones": 0,               no counter-battery drones
"weapons.tank_shell.damage": 120,    one-shot a jeep, two-shot a tank
"weapons.heli_cannon.life": 4,       seconds of flight (speed x life = reach)
"vehicles.tank.speed": 12,           top speed in m/s
"vehicles.jeep.can_carry_flag": 0,   nobody can capture, for a sandbox game
Run `node tools/config-options.mjs` for the full list of 416 names (a word filters, e.g. heli; --json for machine-readable output).
